classification.difficultyReason: The intended solution finds BD first, then uses it with AB to find AD; the printed diagram omits an essential right-angle condition.

content.prompt: Find the length of the side $AD$ in the diagram below.

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD with internal diagonal BD. Single ticks identify BC = CD; double ticks identify AB = BD. Only angle BCD has a right-angle square. AD is drawn vertically, without adding any perpendicularity mark.
spec.mathematics: BC = CD = 3 m; AB = BD; angle BCD = 90 degrees. No right angle at B is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and equality marks are supplied givens; no calculated lengths or additional angle marks are shown.

answer.short:
The marked givens do not determine $AD$ uniquely.

The intended answer is $6\ \mathrm{m}$ if $\angle ABD=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $BCD$, by Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}BD^2&=3^2+3^2\\BD^2&=18\\BD&=\sqrt{18}\ \mathrm{m}.\end{align*}$$
The matching ticks give $AB=BD=\sqrt{18}\ \mathrm{m}$. These lengths alone do not determine $AD$ because no angle of triangle $ABD$ is specified.

If the intended missing condition is $\angle ABD=90^\circ$, then:
$$\begin{align*}AD^2&=AB^2+BD^2\\AD^2&=18+18\\AD^2&=36\\AD&=6\ \mathrm{m}.\end{align*}$$
